votes.reason: No paper found through 2026-09-01 that intervenes on the same object (cumulative log-decay F(s) and write mass W(s) of GDN/KDA/Mamba gates over translation-aligned spans) with the same objective (cross-lingual parity via a parallel-data auxiliary loss or a parity-constrained shared clock), nor one that reports the phase-0 per-language decay ledger R_D vs fertility on released linear-RNN checkpoints. Coverage: arXiv API x4 (linear attention/SSM x multilingual x decay/gate/tokenization; only Falcon-H1 and RWKV-7 surface, neither reports per-language gate statistics), HF papers x2, OpenReview x1, DDG x3 (returned empty; treat as not covered), WebSearch x13, WebFetch on 10 abstracts. Closest priors and why they do not refute: (1) Tallec and Ollivier 2018 (1804.11188) prove gated RNN gates give quasi-invariance to time warps and propose chrono-init; a fertility ratio is exactly such a warp, so this is the theoretical basis the proposal must cite, and it makes the phase-0 self-normalization kill condition plausible (LM loss alone may already learn the warp) but it contains no cross-lingual supervision or measurement. (2) Mamba (2312.00752) Delta_t is already a content-dependent step size/clock; arm (ii)'s shared content clock c_t is a recombination of Mamba Delta with GDN gating and should be written as such; the novelty there is only the parity-constrained totals loss, not the parameterization. (3) MAGNET (2407.08818), H-Net (2507.07955), H-Net++ (2508.05628), Adaptive Targeted Dynamic Chunking (2605.30080) enforce equitable or learned semantic granularity at the segmentation level (H-Net's dynamic chunking is effectively an end-to-end semantic clock with multilingual/Chinese gains) but change the tokenizer/inference path; the proposal keeps the tokenizer fixed and touches only training. (4) Content-dependent decay without cross-lingual supervision: Adaptive Memory Decay for Log-Linear Attention (2605.06946), Kathleen content-dependent reverb (2604.07969), Gated DeltaNet-2 erase/write decoupling (2605.22791, which independently motivates separate F and W ledgers), Elucidating the Design Space of Decay (2509.05282), Optimal Decay Spectra/PoST (2604.07658), Stuffed Mamba (2410.07145) — none has a language or fertility axis. (5) Tokenizer-tax literature (2605.24718 Tokenizer Tax across 25 European languages; Token Tax AfricaNLP 2026; Beyond Fertility STRR) quantifies fertility inequity at the tokenizer/eval level, not inside the recurrent operator. (6) Cross-lingual consistency regularization (2306.06919 CrossConST; Soft Token Alignment 2606.26466) applies parallel-data auxiliary losses to representations/output distributions, not gate statistics; 2603.29026 finds parallel data barely moves representations, which the proposal already pre-registers as a distinct observable. (7) Futrell et al. 2020 lossy-context surprisal derives language-dependent forgetting from language-independent memory limits — conceptual precedent for the phenomenon, no architecture intervention. (8) Probe instruments exist (MLNeedle 2408.10151; Evaluating Multilingual Long-Context Models 2409.18006) but are transformer-focused and do not replot recall against content vs token distance. Residual uncertainty: full texts of Kimi Linear, Falcon-H1, GDN-2 and the RWKV-7 multilingual sections were not read for incidental per-language gate analyses; DDG route was dead and Semantic Scholar unavailable. The idea is a non-trivial recombination (new observable plus new supervision target) rather than a republished mechanism, but the proposal should downgrade what_is_new for arm (ii) and cite 1804.11188 and Mamba Delta as direct ancestors.

The pilot as written cannot separate the stated mechanism (a span-aligned semantic clock supplied by parallel translation data) from its strongest control, and the headline effect is confounded upstream of the gate. (1) Strongest control collapses onto the treatment. The aligned parity loss sum (F_a-F_b)^2/(F_a+F_b) is satisfied to first order by a per-language rescaling of log-decay by the mean fertility ratio, which is exactly the monolingual fertility-scaled-gate oracle; in the P3 synthetic arm (coarse vs 2x finer English tokenization, near-constant ratio) the two are identical by construction, so the one clean identification arm cannot evidence the parallel view. P4 reserves a 70-95% recovery window (~1.5 EM points of a ~6-point gain) to declare the view necessary; 3 seeds at 100M cannot resolve that. (2) The shuffled-pair placebo is not inert: shuffling preserves language marginals, so each F(s_b) is pushed toward E[F(s_a)] and vice versa; the fixed point equalizes cross-language mean decay through the same channel, so the pre-registered "placebo closes <15%" is unlikely and a closing placebo is uninterpretable. (3) Shortcut: with F_a=c*x, F_b=c*y, L=c(x-y)^2/(x+y) has dL/dc>0, so arm (i) is minimized by shrinking all forgetting (alpha->1), a "forget less" regularizer that improves short-range recall regardless of language parity; arm (i) has no anchor and no uniform-decay-regularizer control exists; the +1% BPB tolerance absorbs the cost. (4) The baseline gap is a tokenizer effect with no clock-free bound. Fertility-correlated cross-lingual gaps are established in transformers that have no decay clock (Rust et al. 2021: tokenizer adequacy as important as pretraining data size; Petrov et al. 2023: up to 15x token-length disparities). The pilot's fixed-regex byte-BPE inherits the GPT-2 word regex; 2608.26449 shows that for abugidas this alone produces 1.47x-9.02x fertility and a mark-aware regex repairs it, so much of the pilot's "fertility" is pre-tokenization breakage; the parity-aware-BPE baseline (2606.15044) is absent. The proposed SWA+sinks control (2608.28444) is a fixed token window, i.e. itself a per-token clock, so it cannot bound the non-clock share; a full-attention arm at matched tokenizer/data is missing, and EM across morphologically rich languages adds surface-form variance parity cannot touch. (5) Alternative mechanism not separated: recall in linear models is bounded by state size/key interference (Arora et al. 2024), which scales with token count independent of decay; and because beta appears in both the erase and write terms of GDN (coupling GDN-2, 2605.22791, exists to remove), W-parity also changes erase, so F- and W-parity are not independent knobs and are not separately ablated. Phase 0 is a valid pre-registered kill, but its recall probe on released checkpoints is causally uninterpretable given per-language data and tokenizer disparities. Coverage: one arXiv API query, two web searches, and the pre-pulled feeds found no prior per-language decay ledger for GDN/KDA/Mamba, so novelty is not the objection; identification is. A salvageable version needs a full-attention arm, a mark-aware/parity-BPE tokenizer arm, a uniform decay-regularizer arm, an anchored arm (i), and a pre-registered equivalence test against the monolingual oracle with >=5 seeds.

The pilot is under-costed and, as scoped inside 16 GPU-h, not decisive. (1) Budget: 6 arms x 3 seeds x 1.5B tokens = 27B tokens in 14.4 GPU-h requires 521k tok/s per H100 for a 100M pure GDN plus auxiliary gate loss, i.e. 31.6% 6ND-MFU -- identical to the ~31.5% MFU the GDN authors report for 1.3B models on H100 (~40 Kt/s at 2K, Fig. 3 of 2412.06464; ~40 Kt/s in GDN-2 Fig. 2). Small models run at lower MFU and fla's own README benchmark shows chunk_gdn fwd+bwd is 2.3-4.1x slower than FlashAttention-2 at small (B,T,H,D). Public calibrations: NVlabs 0.4B GDN-H1 on 15B tokens = 4 nodes x 8 GPUs for ~4 h => ~33k tok/s/GPU; the flame-trained 358M pure GDN (puigde) = 15.03B tokens in 9.3 h on 8xA100-40GB => 56k tok/s/GPU (39% of A100 peak). Extrapolated to 100M on H100 this is ~130-450k tok/s => 17-58 GPU-h for the 18 runs alone. The stated budget is 15.9/16 with zero margin and omits the per-arm 30M LR sweep (a listed control), evaluation, tokenizer training, P3's coarse/finer-tokenization arms (>=12 more runs) and all P4/Phase-1b arms, so the 16 GPU-h pilot can test at most P1-P2 and only at best-case MFU. (2) Decisiveness: the identification arm (P3, synthetic-fertility English) is the only thing separating the tokenization clock from per-language competence -- under equal-byte mixing high-fertility languages get far less content (measured NTREX bytes/English: hin 2.71x, ben 2.63x, tam 3.42x) -- and it is unbudgeted, so a P2 gap cannot be attributed to the clock. Three of five Phase-0 checkpoints cannot support the R_D self-normalization ledger: fla-hub/delta_net-1.3B-8K-100B is ungated DeltaNet (fla's DeltaNet layer has beta and an optional output gate only, no alpha_t, so D is identically 0); state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf is Pile/English-only; the startlux cards state training-language composition is undisclosed. Only Qwen3.5-4B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Base are valid subjects. The P2 endpoint is not operationalized (no content-distance grid, item counts, needle/query language or aggregation, unlike the repo's own YAML template), the 6 languages are unnamed, and the 150M-token parallel-view training source is unnamed (FLORES-plus/NTREX are ~53-58k English tokens per language on these tokenizers, ~3 orders of magnitude too small; NLLB/OPUS appears only in the safety field). What does check out: every named model ID exists; Qwen3.5-4B is a 3:1 GDN hybrid whose fla layer exposes A_log/dt_bias (hookable) and fla 0.5.2 exists (2026-07-27, pinned by the startlux checkpoints); FLORES-plus (gated auto), NTREX, FineWeb-2, NLLB/OPUS exist so sentence-level parallel data is supported; measured NTREX fertility on the Qwen3.5-4B tokenizer shows competent languages clearing the pre-registered thresholds (pol 1.61, fin 1.63, hun 1.71, ukr 1.79, hin 2.07, ell 2.12, ben 2.17), so the ~1.5 GPU-h Phase-0 kill gate is cheap and decisive on Qwen3.5-4B/Kimi-Linear; Tinker is not needed. Repair path: re-cost Phase 1 at 25-40 GPU-h, fold P3 into the pilot, drop delta_net/mamba/startlux from the R_D ledger (keep W only), name the 6 languages, the NLLB/OPUS parallel source, and the recall endpoint's grid and aggregation.

claim: GDN/KDA/Mamba gates forget and write once per token, so equal content costs high-fertility languages more forgetting and write mass; a training-time parallel-translation view equalizing cumulative log-decay and write mass over aligned spans (auxiliary loss on gate statistics, or a shared content clock with parity-constrained totals) removes the inequity and equalizes translation-paired recall at unchanged per-language BPB with no inference change; a training-free phase 0 first tests whether released gates already self-normalize.

votes.reason: Searched arXiv (9 queries), HF papers (4), OpenReview (2; result pages blocked by browser check), DDG (4; returned empty on this route), plus 7 WebSearch queries and full-text WebFetch of the DSA and QSA papers. No paper was found that (a) supervises a detached top-k sparse-attention indexer (DSA/QSA/LSA/MSA class) with a cross-lingual alignment target, or (b) reports per-language / cross-lingual recall of such an indexer. Full text of DeepSeek-V3.2 (2512.02556) and Qwen3.8-Next (2608.30320) confirms the indexer is trained by KL to main attention only (dense warm-up + sparse-stage KL, no auxiliary loss) and neither paper contains any cross-lingual or per-language analysis of the indexer (QSA reports only aggregate MMMLU). LongCat LSA (2608.01662) uses cross-layer distillation, not an external alignment target. HySparse (2602.03560) replaces the indexer with the preceding full-attention layer as oracle, no bilingual signal. MLNeedle (2408.10151) and OneRuler (2503.01996) document the cross-lingual long-context gap in dense models but do not localize it to a component or propose a fix; the withdrawn Retrieval-Transition Heads paper (2602.22453) finds dense retrieval heads are largely shared across languages, which is consistent with (not a refutation of) the claim that a low-rank indexer, not dense attention, would be the cross-lingual bottleneck. Why confidence is only 0.6: the mechanism is a recognizable recombination of 'supervised/guided attention' from NMT (Liu et al. 2016, 1609.04186; Chen et al. 2016 guided alignment: aligner-derived alignments used as a training-time-only supervision on attention, inference unchanged) applied to a 2025-class indexer with bilingual concatenated contexts; a reviewer could call this a straightforward transfer, and the 'exceeds dense teacher' moonshot is unsupported by any prior. Coverage limits: OpenReview forum pages could not be read (Cloudflare check), DDG returned nothing, no Semantic Scholar/full-text search of LongCat, MiniMax MSA, or A.X K2 for per-language tables, and no ACL Anthology search. Novelty therefore holds under this coverage; P1 (diagnostic: indexer recall gap cross-script vs mono) appears to be untested in the literature and is the load-bearing new claim.

Identification failure: the pilot as written cannot separate the stated mechanism (a KL-only indexer distilled from full attention is the cross-lingual selection bottleneck, fixed by translation supervision of the indexer) from at least five stronger alternative explanations, and its primary metric leaks the training labels. (1) Circular metric: L_x maximizes indexer mass on aligner-derived sets A(t); 'aligned-block recall@k' is the same aligner's A(t), so P1/P2 in that metric measure aligner imitation, not whether selection is the NIAH bottleneck; only generation EM is non-circular. (2) Retrofit-vs-architecture: Phase 1 is a frozen Qwen3-0.6B-Base plus KL indexer, whereas DSA freezes the backbone only for a 2.1B-token warm-up and then trains 943.7B tokens unfrozen at k=2048, and QSA distills ~2B tokens then trains 'the entire backbone under the guidance of the indexer'; SpotAttention (2606.22874) already publishes the frozen-Qwen3 KL-only selector arm (4 heads x 128, softmax-then-mean teacher) at dense parity on English RULER at 128K with non-English explicitly untested; the from-scratch arm (Phase 1b) is conditional, so nothing decisive is 'architecture-causal'. (3) Token-budget confound at fixed top-k: the Qwen3 tokenizer (vocab 151,669 = Qwen2.5) is classified letters-only pre-tokenization with a 9.02x Thai shatter multiplier (Hangul/Han 1.00x), Qwen2.5 Chinese is 0.71 chars/token vs English 3.77, Hindi carries 4.45x under Qwen2.5; aligned blocks and haystacks in th/zh occupy different token counts per unit content so recall@k and NIAH at fixed k move with script mechanically. Lost in Compression (2608.26175) shows selection quality can only be isolated with achieved-token-budget matching in the target tokenizer; RTPurbo shows fixed top-k vs top-p alone shifts RULER-64K 70.53 to 85.49, larger than the predicted 15-point gap; no per-language budget-matched or top-p control is listed. (4) Unmatched alternative for the 'indexer gap': DSA/QSA KL targets sum attention across all heads (QSA adds max-pooling because signals are 'diluted during aggregation'); retrieval heads are <5% of heads (2404.15574) and a 16-d projector recovers >90% retrieval recall (RTPurbo), so rank-128 capacity is not binding; P1 never measures the head-summed target's own aligned recall (the KL-only ceiling), so it cannot separate indexer, target construction, and teacher. (5) L_x vs the 'mandatory data control' is an information asymmetry: KL-only-bilingual never sees aligner labels while L_x injects OmniAlign (0.3B mGTE, LaBSE distillation on 6.82M pairs, human-annotated SFT); there is no dense-backbone-plus-alignment-supervision control at matched compute, and Lost in Compression found the cross-lingual selection gap 'tracks supervision data, not architecture'. (6) P3 (sparse exceeds dense) is a generic denoising effect already shown without any alignment supervision: QSA lifts RULER 512K-1M 90.08 to 93.00 and MRCR-512K 30.66 to 40.53; FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4 reports an 'attention denoiser' gain at 13.5% KV; the counterfactual audit (2608.01676) shows sparse amplification up to delta +0.93; no oracle or random-plus-needle selection control. (7) Label noise correlated with treatment: OmniAlign AER Ja-En 29.6 vs Fr-En 2.7 (Zh-En 8.5); awesome-align Ja-En 37.4 vs Fr-En 4.1; no ko/th AER reported, so both supervision and metric are noisier exactly where the gap is predicted. (8) Contamination path: MLNeedle needles are MLQA (Wikipedia) with mMARCO Wikipedia haystacks while training uses WikiMatrix; no dedup specified. (9) Dense ceiling: MLNeedle 7-8B instruct models score 0.24-0.30 on non-Latin needles at 4K vs 0.68 English, and OneRuler shows up to 20% cross-lingual swing from instruction language plus 'none' over-prediction (non-retrieval components); no cross-lingual long-context number exists for Qwen3-0.6B, so '+10 EM within the frozen ceiling' may be infeasible. Prior-art note: alignment-supervised attention is established NMT practice (Liu et al. 2016; Garg et al. 2019), omitted from 'what is new'. Salvageable only with: per-language achieved-budget or top-p control, retrieval-head-weighted/max-pooled KL target control, dense+alignment-supervised LoRA control, oracle-selection control, an aligner-independent recall metric (needle-token recall), and WikiMatrix/ParaCrawl dedup against eval sets. Coverage limits: no per-language DSA/QSA selection analysis found via WebSearch or arXiv host query; Semantic Scholar unavailable; Qwen tokenizer not runnable locally; a Qwen3 RULER table extraction returned duplicated rows and was discarded.

The pilot is not runnable as a decisive <=16 GPU-h screen with the named data, models and harness. (1) Parallel-data assumption unsupported: the repo's own 2026-09-01 program lists the parallel-corpus inventory (pairs, alignment granularity, segment lengths, license) as a blocking input and states "the repository contains no parallel corpus at all" (research/frontier-systems-program-2026-09-01.md:124); Stage 1 G13 indexer probes are gated behind that inventory and a <=16 GPU-h/screen cap (line 134), and synthesis.md:403 makes G13 conditional on a prior G2 result. The named public sources do not supply "8K aligned-document contexts" for en<->zh/ko: WikiMatrix is mined parallel sentences (135M sentences, no documents; arXiv 1907.05791); ParaCrawl bonus en-ko/en-th ship only as TXT/TMX/Dedup sentence pairs (paracrawl.eu/moredata); the document-recovered ParaDocs release covers en-th but neither en-ko nor en-zh (HF jhu-clsp/paradocs dirs). The named frozen aligners exist but have no validated ko/th coverage: OmniAlign is optimized for zh/es/it/de/fr/ru (HF tags zh,en,de,fr,es,it,ru,ja,pt,ro; 8192-token max), CTFAlign ships tuned layers only for en-fr/ro/ja/zh, la-gr, with best AER 0.518 on en-ja and 0.255 on en-zh, so A(t) labels for the P1 recall endpoint on th/ko are unvalidated and noisy. (2) Claimed harness pieces do not exist: the "UOT doctor" (harness/translation_boundaries.py) is a NumPy, model-free reference whose docstring says a production run must replace it with a differentiable solver, so the L_eq arm has no loss implementation; the repo's "exact-match harness" is tool_call_exact_match for tau-bench (experiments/pilot_01_tau_bench.yaml), and grep finds no NIAH/RULER/needle code; pyproject has no fla/flash-attn and no sparse-attention or indexer code. fla ships only fla/ops/dsa/naive.py (191 lines, einsum reference) which materializes 16 x T^2 scores per layer: at 32K that is 34 GB bf16 (69 GB fp32 softmax) per layer, so the 32K NIAH/RULER endpoint cannot run without writing a chunked kernel. (3) Budget: with 200M tokens = 24,414 x 8K sequences and explicit per-layer 8192^2 attention probabilities for the KL target, one teacher stream is ~5.5e17 FLOPs plus ~0.4 TB/seq of memory traffic (~1.5 GPU-h at ~300 TFLOPS effective) and each of the 12 indexers ~0.6 GPU-h; the stated 9 GPU-h only holds if the teacher pass is shared across arms (unstated; the harness convention is one sbatch job per arm, giving ~25 GPU-h). L_eq via Sinkhorn over 8K x 8K per aligned query is ~5e18 FLOPs (>5 GPU-h, worse memory-bound) unless subsampled (unspecified). Eval of ~15 arms on cross/mono NIAH plus RULER-en at 8K-32K adds roughly 10-40 GPU-h; detecting the P2 "+10 EM" with SE ~7 points at n=100/cell needs several hundred samples per cell. (4) Decisiveness: DSA's frozen-model KL warm-up (2.1B tokens) is never deployed as-is; production indexers are followed by 943.7B tokens of sparse adaptation of all parameters (arXiv 2512.02556) and QSA trains at CPT over ~200B tokens (2608.30320), so EM deltas on a frozen Qwen3-0.6B at k=12.5% conflate sparse-shock with selection. The dense 0.6B teacher's cross-lingual NIAH at 8K-32K is undocumented (model card gives 28 layers, 16Q/8KV, 32K, no long-context evals); 7-8B models already fall from 0.68 to 0.30 (zh) / 0.24 (ar) at 4K on MLNeedle, and 0.5B-class models average 22-44% on monolingual NIAH (arXiv 2409.15790), so headroom for P2/P3 is unestablished. (5) Tinker boundary: TINKER_API_KEY is absent, tinker==0.23.3 is stale (service rejects unsupported SDKs), GLM-5.3 context tiers are unfrozen, and no internals are exposed, so the "production behavioral baseline" cannot run now. What survives: all cited control/aligner papers are real (PIVOT 2607.24593, RouteSparse 2608.29058, SWA+sinks 2608.28444, LongCat LSA 2608.01662, OmniAlign, CTFAlign), and P1 (attention-mass recall) is measurable on en-th via ParaDocs plus fla's naive DSA reference; a re-scoped en-th-only P1 screen with shared teacher passes could fit, but that is not the pilot as written.

claim: Learned sparse-attention indexers (DSA/QSA class) distilled only from full attention are a cross-lingual retrieval bottleneck; supervising the indexer with aligned bilingual documents (a view that never touches main attention) makes selection language-invariant, closes most of the cross-lingual needle gap at fixed top-k, and can exceed the dense teacher on cross-lingual retrieval.

votes.reason: Searched 30+ queries (arXiv API x14, hfpapers x5, openreview x3, ddg x7 — ddg returned empty every time, a coverage gap) plus WebFetch on 15 abstracts. No paper was found that trains a Mixture-of-Depths router with a parallel-pair compute-parity penalty or reports a FLOPs-per-aligned-sentence ledger, so the MoD half of the claim is not directly occupied. However the candidate fails the "same object, same objective" test on its pooling knob and reads as a recombination of published pieces: (1) MAGNET (arXiv 2407.08818, NeurIPS 2024) already trains learned boundary predictors inside a byte-level LM with the explicit objective of equitable segmentation granularity across languages/scripts and reports faster language modelling — i.e. a model-internal length/compute knob optimized for cross-lingual parity; the candidate's Knob 2 differs only in anchoring the target via parallel-pair counts instead of per-script predictors. (2) Parity-aware BPE (2508.04796) already defines the per-language cost-parity objective (fair-max, Gini of per-language token cost) and is listed by the candidate itself as a control, so the "parity" objective is published; moving it from the tokenizer to a MoD router (2404.02258) is a regularizer swap on an existing router, and for dense/MoD models token count already is the FLOPs ledger that 'Do All Languages Cost the Same?' (2305.13707) and the Token Tax line report per language. (3) Dynamic Token Pooling (2211.09761), H-Net and FlexiTokens (2507.12720) already supply the boundary-head/ratio-loss machinery; FlexiTokens explicitly argues against fixed-rate targets, which is exactly the space the candidate's 'parity-count' target occupies. (4) Multilingual MoE routing work (2510.04694, SARA 2606.25821, 2605.29714) covers the expert knob's cross-lingual side, leaving only unit-normalized load balancing, a minor tweak. What survives as genuinely unfound is the parallel-pair-anchored FLOPs-per-aligned-sentence ledger and applying it to MoD depth routing — a measurement/objective contribution rather than a new architecture, and per the lens's default-to-refuted rule under uncertainty, the mechanism should be treated as an incremental recombination (MAGNET objective + MoD knob + Parity-BPE metric) unless the Phase-0 ledger shows an effect the tokenizer-level fix cannot reproduce.

The Phase-1 pilot cannot distinguish the stated mechanism (meaning-indexed compute via a parallel-pair parity penalty) from its strongest matched control, and its headline number is a ledger artifact.

1) Missing matched control. The registered primary endpoint rho(L)=mean_pairs C(x_L)/C(x_en) is a per-language MEAN. The penalty E_pairs[(log C_A - log C_B)^2] decomposes into (E log C_A - E log C_B)^2 + Var(log C_A - log C_B); only the mean term moves rho, and it needs no parallel data at all: a language-ID-conditioned threshold tau_{l,L} (or a language-mean parity penalty on monolingual batches) reaches the same rho by construction. This arm is absent from the arm list (dense, MoD-uniform, parity-MoD, heuristic-skip, parity-BPE, GRT). The shuffled-pair "placebo" does not fill the gap: it keeps the same mean-matching term (so it also drives rho toward 1) and adds a within-language length-variance term that damages quality, so "aligned beats shuffled" would be explained by the placebo's extra damage, not by meaning-indexing. Per-language/script rate schedules are already the standard practice (MAGNET per-script predictors 2407.08818; Nawrot et al. hand-set boundary priors alpha=0.2 en/vi/he vs 0.37 fi, 2211.09761; MrT5 emergent per-language deletion rates via PI controller 2410.20771), and the "unsupervised rates already equalize" kill is deferred to the conditional 1b arm rather than the funding gate. 2603.29026 (parallel data adds little to alignment) is the prior the candidate itself cites.

2) Ledger omits the dominant unroutable cost. C(x)=sum_t sum_l r_{t,l} c_l counts only routed blocks. At the pilot's d=512, 12 layers, 32k vocab, the unembedding matmul is 2*V*d=32.8 MFLOP/token vs 88 MFLOP full-depth routed cost (27% of per-token FLOPs), scales with token count, and cannot be routed away. With fertility F=3.0 and a 50% token-weighted budget the minimum TRUE rho is 1.54 (c_en=1.0, c_L=0.33) while the candidate's ledger reports 1.00; at F=3.5 it is 1.86 vs 1.25. P2's "rho <= 1.4 from 2.0-3.5" is therefore unreachable in real FLOPs or an artifact of the ledger definition. The motivating inequity (Petrov 2305.15425; Ahia 2305.13707) is tokens billed, decode latency, and context, none of which depth routing changes.

3) Soft-train/hard-infer routing breaks iso-FLOPs and the dense control. The design note defines training as soft MoD (h^{(l)}=h^{(l-1)}+r*Block) with hard skipping only at inference: every MoD arm trains at dense-12L FLOPs with full-length attention, the parity penalty acts on a soft expected cost that never equals inference cost, and the "dense iso-total-FLOP" arm (narrowed to the 50% FLOP count) has ~half the parameters and half the training compute of every MoD arm (MoD's own paper: isoFLOP-optimal MoD models are "bigger"). The kill "iso-FLOP dense beats every adaptive arm by >2%" is biased against triggering. At inference MoD's residual path excludes skipped tokens from attention entirely (2404.02258), a regime never trained; any BPB loss is then misattributed to (or masked for) the parity mechanism, or if KV is kept the FLOPs ledger is wrong.

4) The premise is at the wrong position. P1 measures the entropy of predicting continuation tokens, which is low in every language and tokenizer (word-internal subword surprisal: 2310.17774, 2412.11940), so a "pass" is non-diagnostic. In a causal LM the compute at position t predicts t+1 and supplies K/V to all later positions; MoD's own analysis ties routing to the entropy of the prediction made AT the position, i.e. the easy positions are the ones preceding continuations, not the continuation tokens. Kaplan et al. 2410.05864, cited by the design note for "detokenization", show whole-word representations are assembled at the LAST subword token in early/middle layers: continuation positions are where word-identity compute happens. Reaching rho<=1.4 at F=3 requires c_L~0.33-0.39, i.e. near-total skipping of >=50% of bn/ta/th tokens, which removes them from attention and deletes word identity from context. P1's second half (aligned-unit CV<=10%) is near-tautological because units are English-anchored aligner spans (repo translation_boundaries.py SpanLink); P1's models (Qwen3 151k, SmolLM2 49k vocab) and the repo fertility harness (tiktoken) do not share the pilot's 32k byte-BPE, so P1 does not transfer to the pilot substrate.

5) Knob 3 cannot test the claim: a fixed top-2 MoE uses exactly k experts per token, so unit-normalized load balancing leaves C(x) unchanged; 1c measures expert specialization, not compute parity. Secondary: 2 seeds at 60M for a 1% per-language BPB margin on a 7-language mix is underpowered (DataDecide used 3 seeds and reports run-to-run SD up to 2 points at 1B; small-scale noise uncharacterized).

At the pilot's scale the "few-shot-over-zero-shot gain" is dominated by label-space/format recognition, not input-label learning: Min et al. (2202.12837) show random labels barely hurt ICL; Pan, Gao, Chen & Chen (2305.09731, Kevin's own advisor's lab) show 350M models get ~10 points from 8 demonstrations via task recognition alone, that this plateaus with scale, and that genuine task learning appears only at OPT-66B/davinci; Wei et al. (2303.03846) show small models ignore flipped labels. R_theta plus the jointly fitted P/Q is trained on ICL families and can therefore encode the label-space/format prior in theta and in the read map Q (label-word directions are the ICL extraction channel, 2305.14160), whereas delta/Kaczmarz/OSDN/Falcon have no parameters to hold such a prior. A ">=70% vs <=40%" gap is thus the expected signature of "trainable module vs parameter-free rule on the same task distribution," not of distillation. The controls that would identify the mechanism are absent: random-label (TR-only) demonstrations, held-out task *format* families disjoint from distillation, and a same-interface rule trained directly on labels compared head-to-head (the "prequential sibling" only appears in Phase 2; if it ties, distillation added nothing; if distilled wins, soft targets explain it). The pilot also never states that distillation queries/families are disjoint from the "sealed" evaluation families, so the teacher's own few-shot predictions on evaluation-family queries may be training targets for theta/P/Q.

2) The Phase-1 denominator is empirically near zero or negative at pythia-160m, so P1 is unmeasurable there. Pythia's own Tables 7 and 11 (2304.01373): 160M zero-shot -> five-shot is LAMBADA 0.342->0.268 (few-shot hurts), PIQA 0.618->0.620, WinoGrande 0.497->0.513, WSC 0.365->0.365, ARC-E 0.440->0.453, ARC-C 0.201->0.205, LogiQA 0.210->0.237, with SEs of 0.010-0.047; only SciQ (0.720->0.792) moves, a multiple-choice format effect. Note also that the candidate misstates this paper: the full text does not list segmented ingestion or streaming certificates as future work (Sections 9-10 discuss scale/scope only). (2) The frozen-base "ridge/commutative statistics" substrate with exact one-shot forgetting is Larimar (ICML 2024, arXiv 2403.11901): frozen decoder + Kanerva-style pseudoinverse least-squares memory where forgetting with alpha=-1 yields "the least-squares solution with Z_forgot removed from the data" — exact deletion equal to never-written, on a frozen LLM, uncited by the candidate. (3) The affine-composition algebra of the (gated) delta rule and its associative/tree structure is standard (DeltaNet chunkwise WY, 2406.06484; TreeWY, 2608.20961); a segment tree over affine maps for O(log N) exclusion is textbook parallel-scan machinery, and independent per-record encoding is APE/Block-Attention (2502.05431). Composing these yields the candidate's Substrate 1/2 without a new architectural idea beyond "make the memory the only long-range channel", which is the same reason kNN/Memorizing-Transformer and plain linear-attention stores are trivially deletable. (4) "Unlearning by design" memory-augmented transformers with exact key deletion (MUNKEY, 2603.15033) and certified/exact-unlearning SV memory (Forgetful Attention, 2607.12204) already occupy the "deletable memory by construction" niche; certified per-record influence bounds against memory poisoning exist for agent memory (SMSR, 2606.12703). What survives as genuinely unfound: an iso-FLOP price of record-independence vs a GDN 3:1 hybrid, exact leave-one-out attribution on fast weights, and typed norm-capped write channels on fast-weight state — but these are measurements/engineering on top of known mechanisms, not a new mechanism, so under the stated default (same object+objective => refuted) this candidate is refuted as a recombination. The algebra is sound but already someone else's control, and the pilot as written cannot attribute any of P2-P4 to the stated mechanism rather than to its strongest matched controls.

1) P1 reproduces a published control. 2607.27539 v2 (Aug 13 2026) states Proposition 1 as a fixed-suffix transport identity and runs a fixed-input control that freezes later (k, v, gates) after omission, reaching 6.1e-6 relative error; its native-KDA 12-49% suffix change (median forcing-to-difference ratio 0.84) is the candidate's "state-reading write deviates >=5%" control. The associativity itself is the WY/Householder chunkwise training algebra (2406.06484), reused by TreeWY (2608.20961), and Log-Linear Attention already keeps a Fenwick-tree hierarchy of GDN states (2506.04761). Phase 0 therefore adds no identifying evidence; everything rests on P2-P4.

2) P2 (frozen route) is tautological or leaky and has no stored-recall floor. For a fast-weight sidecar on a frozen base, "never-stored" can only mean S recomposed over the other 199 records, which the algebra makes identical to the deleted state up to fp error, so KL<=1e-6 restates P1. If any fitted component (write head, read projection, APE temperatures/scales) saw record j, deleting from S leaves the imprint 2607.27539 documents for its conditional certificate (it needed full repack; 66.5% of 4B boundary decrements fell back to exact refit). Substrate 1's APE-style document-blocked prefill keeps per-record KV blocks that are already exactly deletable by dropping the block (the O(N)-bytes kNN/KV control): if KV is retained, S is redundant for both recall and exact deletion; if KV is discarded, recall flows through a lightly trained ridge read on a frozen 0.6B base, and Beyond Perplexity (2607.00368) found one-step writes on Qwen3 lower loss while free-form recall stays at zero. P2 has no precondition that stored recall is high, so a memory that stores nothing passes "deleted equals never-stored within 1 pt". No S-off / KV-only ablation is listed. The gradient-ascent comparison is cross-substrate: TOFU stores knowledge in fine-tuned weights where all baselines fail (2401.06121); the fast-weight route never touches weights.

3) Retrofit-vs-architecture confusion in the gate. "Blocking costs <=5 pts RULER, >10 kills the frozen route" on a frozen, sequentially trained Qwen3-0.6B-Base measures the parallel-encoding penalty (APE 2502.05431: naive parallel encoding trails APE by 3.6-7.9%, APE itself retains only 98%/93% of sequential; Block-Attention 2409.15355 needs fine-tuning to match full attention) plus reader immaturity. That penalty is independent of the delta-rule memory, yet Substrate 2 is conditional on it, so the architectural claim is admitted or killed by a retrofit artifact.

4) P3 anchors LM loss to a mismatched control. The GDN 3:1 hybrid is 3 GDN : 1 full global attention (Kimi Linear 2510.26692: 3 KDA layers per full MLA layer, added precisely because pure linear attention fails long-context retrieval). The read-free band has no global attention and one write layer, so any gap conflates the read-free constraint with missing full attention, single vs stacked memory, and HP transfer. The matched control (writer-reads-band) is in the grid but the prediction anchors it only on MQAR (<=3 pts), a single-hop task that never needs writer-side memory. The capability the constraint removes is documented: Just Read Twice (2407.05483) shows recurrent recall depends on ordering and on selecting what to store given earlier state/question; a memory-free writer cannot condition writes on the question, earlier records, or coreference, and neither MQAR nor S-NIAH measures this (RULER variable-tracking chains longer than R, repeated-context, cross-record coreference would). SWA+sinks (2608.28444) already matches post-trained linear attention and is 2-10x on NIAH/BABILong, so the LM-loss window at 60M/1.0B tokens is too narrow to attribute. The grid (60M/135M x 3 seeds x 1.0B tokens, about 7-17N) sits far below the program's own believability bar (>=256 tuned configs per scale, >=3 sizes, ~1000N, SWA+sinks and tail-replay controls); 2606.15378 shows hybrids converge under sufficient training and long-range retrieval is carried by full attention, so small-budget gaps are training-speed, not capability, signals.

5) P4 is by construction and confounded. The influence detector scores ||A_D - I|| and ||B_D||; trigger/erase poisons are defined as records with large such norms, so AUROC>=0.90 vs <=0.60 for plain false facts is definitional. Setting A_t = I for untrusted channels returns those writes to the additive/Hebbian regime whose recall deficit versus the delta rule is the founding result of the DeltaNet line (2102.11174, 2406.06484), so the "<=10 pts benign recall cost" is confounded with the known additive-update penalty; no arm separates cap-cost from erase-removal-cost. The bound ||y(S_N) - y(S_N^(-c))|| <= Gamma_c is on the linear read, not on logits or ASR after the nonlinear frozen stack. 2608.21230 already shows exclusion-style defenses collapse when the correct answer comes from untrusted sources; a uniform cap has the same failure mode and an adaptive split-payload attacker is not among the controls.

6) The audit arm (E2-TTT 2608.21308 checkpoints, FwPKM 2601.00671, SR-TTT self-tests 2603.06642v2) is valid but is the program's existing G6 item and independent of this mechanism.

Fixes that would restore identification: run Substrate 2 unconditionally with writer-reads-band as the primary control on LM loss and on ordering/multi-hop tasks; add a KV-block-drop and S-off ablation plus a pre-deletion exact-match recall floor to P2; add a delta-with-cap untrusted arm to P4. Coverage: abstracts plus the 2607.27539 v2 HTML; six host arXiv queries and three web searches found no other exact-unlearning-in-fast-weights work through 2026-09-01.

The 16 GPU-h figure is itself unsupported: the grid is 7 arms x 3 seeds x 1.0B tokens at 60M = 21 one-billion-token runs, 12 of them custom fast-weight "band" variants with no fla kernel, plus a 135M pair plus HP search. The only published H100 anchor for this model class is E2-TTT's own Appendix B.5 (arXiv 2608.21308v2): a plain-PyTorch fast-weight+SWA hybrid trains at 17.6-20.0 kTPS on one H100 at 340M (LaCT 23.7 kTPS; ~58-70 TFLOPS, i.e. 6-7% of bf16 peak), and 15B tokens cost "about 132 and 348 total GPU hours" at 340M and 1.3B (8.8 GPU-h per 1B tokens at 340M). The repo's own envelope table (research/frontier-systems-program-2026-08-10.md) prices a 100-150M pilot at 2-5B tokens at 40-120 GPU-h, consistent with this. The GDN paper (2412.06464) measures only ~40-50 kTPS per H100 even for fla-kernel GDN/GDN-H1 at 1.3B.

2) Phase 1(b) is not a decisive architecture test. The "TTT-NTP-style write head" (arXiv 2606.21803) is validated only by continued pretraining of the whole backbone at 32K context (0.2B tokens for Qwen3-0.6B-Base; W_proj "trained jointly under the standard next-token CPT loss"), so the "frozen base" substrate has no published precedent and must be re-derived. P2's headline endpoint (post-deletion recall = never-stored within 1 pt, KL <= 1e-6) follows from the affine algebra by construction and is already demonstrated by 2607.27539 (verified deletion agrees with conditional refit within 1.3e-10 max KL on frozen Gemma 3); the KL<=1e-6 bar is also precision-sensitive in bf16. What remains informative is the document-blocking cost on RULER, a parallel-encoding cost measurement of the kind APE (2502.05431, training-free, 93-98% retention) already reports, against Qwen3-0.6B-Base baselines of 81.8/71.0/65.2/56.2 at 4k-32k (from 2606.21803). Arm (c) presupposes a substrate with non-trivial recall, so it is contingent on (b) surviving its own >10-pt kill. Arm (a) is feasible (checkpoints, code and RULER S-NIAH 512-16K eval.sh all released; FwPKM's cross-sample memory carry-over is acknowledged in SakanaAI issue #1) but is a re-run audit, not a test of the mechanism.

3) Parallel-data assumption. The pilot sources "FLORES translations" for poisons, but FLORES-200 (CC-BY-SA 4.0, gated) is a fixed ~1k-sentence-per-language dev set and cannot supply translations of bespoke TOFU-style poison facts; the cross-lingual arm is marked optional and the candidate concedes "No unique data asset otherwise", so Kevin's parallel data is not load-bearing and the FLORES role as written is mis-specified. Tinker is not used, so its boundary is irrelevant.

claim: If a delta-rule fast-weight memory's write inputs come from a memory-free, record-blocked writer, the state is an associative composition of per-record affine maps: exact deletion and reset at O(log N), exact leave-one-out attribution at O(N), attestable receipts, and provable per-record/per-channel influence bounds (untrusted channels write additively, no-erase, norm-capped) — properties native KDA/GDN provably lack; the program prices the constraint on a frozen base and in a from-scratch hybrid against a GDN 3:1 hybrid at iso-FLOP, and audits E2-TTT/FwPKM beyond-window recall under SR-TTT causality tests.

votes.reason: Ran 19 hostsearch.sh queries (11 arXiv, 3 ddg, 4 hfpapers, 1 openreview), 3 WebSearch queries, and WebFetch on 6 papers. No paper found that intervenes on the same object (the recurrent state of a GDN/KDA hybrid, forked per tool-observation and committed via a receipt-gated, logged delta) with the same objective (bitwise containment, exact retraction, order invariance over concurrent tool results). Closest overlaps each cover one piece: 2607.27539 targets auditable deletion receipts on KDA but only reports that native subtraction fails (8-49% residual) and retrofits a support-vector gate into frozen Gemma 3, no fork/commit; CommitKV (2608.07855) uses tool-call commit transitions but only for training-free KV-page eviction in transformers, no recurrent state, retraction, or concurrency; RW-TTT (2605.28053) tags request-owned TTT state with owner/version/READ-WRITE effects for batched serving, no observation-boundary semantics; STree (2505.14969) branches hybrid-SSM state but solely for speculative tree decoding; Set-LLM (2505.15433) achieves permutation invariance via attention masks and shared positions in transformers over set inputs, not recurrent state or tool results; CaMeL (2601.09923) is system-level isolation, not in-model. Surprise-based observation rejection exists in world-model RL (2512.01119, Nous 2606.22030) but via a separate world model, not an action-conditioned forecast of the recurrence's own state delta. Gated DeltaNet-2 (2605.22791) and Erase-then-Delta (2606.26560) decouple erase/write addresses but have no boundary typing or receipt gating. The recombination is not trivial: the receipt-gated commit of Delta_j = Q_j - P with ledger propagation for exact retraction is a specific mechanism not present in any found prior. Caveats lowering confidence: arXiv host queries were highly conjunctive and returned few hits; Semantic Scholar and full-text search unavailable; a mid-2026 paper on typed/sandboxed state in linear RNN agents could exist under different vocabulary. Note also the claim's 'retraction identity' only holds with later inputs fixed (as the mechanism text concedes), so its advantage over checkpoint replay in 2607.27539 is efficiency, not a stronger guarantee.

The pilot as written cannot separate the trained-in fork/commit mechanism from training-free state surgery on a plain GDN/KDA hybrid, and its headline retraction prediction (P2) rests on mixing two different counterfactual references.

1. Retraction is a mis-stated counterfactual, and the tautological half is already prior art on the same model. CGOS's ledger rule (C_j <- A_t C_j; P_T - C_j^(T) equals the g_j=0 state "with later inputs fixed") is Proposition 1 of arXiv 2607.27539 ("frozen-input transport": if present and omitted trajectories receive identical (A_t, b_t) after the boundary, Delta_T = Delta_tau A_{tau+1}...A_T reproduces the omitted state). That paper already implemented subtract + decay-ledger + transport training-free on the frozen Kimi Linear 48B (the very model the proposal lists for P1) and scored them against checkpoint replay, the true omission counterfactual: raw contribution differs 12-49%, still 8-49% after the ledger, because "native omission changes the later transition and write inputs" (median relative k/v/g/beta suffix-input differences 0.150/0.246/0.025/0.088) and "convolution and MLA cache state also change". CGOS does nothing about later inputs changing, so vs replay it inherits the same residual; vs fixed-input transport, plain GDN is already exact by the same linear-recurrence algebra (GDN Eq. 10: S_t = S_{t-1}(alpha_t(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T)) + beta_t v_t k_t^T, transition depends only on the current token). The predicted contrast (CGOS <= 1e-3 relative / KL <= 1e-4 vs "plain GDN drifts >= 10%") can therefore only appear if the two arms are scored against different references; the Phase 0 "retraction identity to 1e-12" is the fixed-input tautology. P1's retraction half (>= 10% shift on frozen hybrids) is likewise already answered by 2607.27539.

2. Containment on abort is a harness/inference property, not an architectural one. Restoring a snapshot of a linear-recurrence state is training-free (TreeWY does exact commit/rollback of GDN state across speculation trees on Qwen3.5-35B/397B; HARTS forks GDN/KDA state at rollout-tree branch points; DeltaLog keeps a base state plus a bounded delta log). "Abort leaves P bitwise unchanged" and "poisoned aborted content adopted 0.0% vs >= 20%" are guaranteed by the harness's valid_j bit and equally by observation masking on the plain hybrid (which the proposal lists only as an evaluation-time control, not a kill). The strongest matched control, an iso-parameter plain hybrid with inference-time fork/restore + ledger + CommitKV-style eviction, is absent from the arm list, so the pilot cannot attribute containment or retraction to training.

3. Order invariance is delivered by a known masking construction plus an additive set-commit that is algebraically unsound, and the pilot cannot tell whether the commit path carries anything. The softmax half (sibling attention masked, shared position id) is Set-LLM's mask + set-positional-encoding recipe. The recurrent half sums sibling deltas: with Q_i = P A_i + W_i, P + sum_i (Q_i - P) = P(sum_i A_i - (n-1)I) + sum_i W_i; for 3 siblings whose composed decay is 0.5 each, the persistent state is multiplied by -0.5. DASC shows GDN/KDA heads and channels have markedly different retention horizons, so short-horizon units hit this on any multi-hundred-token observation, forcing the learned gate toward g -> 0 on those units, and lambda_r ||C_j||^2/||Delta_j||^2 independently pushes g -> 0. The likely equilibrium is that observation information reaches later decisions via the softmax KV (B_obs), with the commit vestigial, so TV = 0 invariance and P3 parity would be properties of masking rather than the mechanism. The arm list has "CGOS without set-commit" and a g ~ 1 kill, but no never-commit (g = 0) arm and no g -> 0 kill.

4. Surprise receipt has an unpre-registered length shortcut. Delta_j = P(A_j - I) + W_j scales with observation length and ||P||; a rank-8 action-conditioned forecast issued before the observation exists cannot know its length, so eps_j and s_j carry a length component. Harness-labelled unexpected/poisoned observations in synthetic worlds differ systematically in length, so AUROC >= 0.90 is consistent with a length shortcut; only position bias is pre-registered, not length-matched AUROC.

Coverage: arXiv abstract/HTML pages via WebFetch and the pre-pulled feeds through 2026-08-31; TreeWY, HARTS, Set-LLM and DASC read at abstract level only; arXiv API and Semantic Scholar unavailable from this machine.

votes.reason: The proposal's core object (per-head attention-level typing of tokens by provenance to stop tool/document content from steering actions) and its two auxiliary claims (a typed value path; an attention-mass provenance monitor) are each already published, and the "no direct prior art" statement misses them. (1) Contextual Integrity Verification (arXiv 2508.09288, Aug 2025, code released) attaches provenance labels to every token from a 5-tier source lattice (SYSTEM > USER > TOOL > DOCUMENT > WEB) and enforces it as a per-head pre-softmax hard attention mask (query_trust >= key_trust else -inf) with optional FFN/residual gating on frozen Llama-3-8B/Mistral-7B, reporting 0% ASR under its threat model with no perplexity loss. This is exactly PTA-hard (gamma[act,obs]=0) generalized to all heads; PTA's learned 6x6 per-head bias table is the soft relaxation of CIV's mask, an incremental delta not a new mechanism. The additive per-segment attention-logit bias on labeled tool segments is also already used causally in 2606.16364 (dose-response on 10 models). (2) The "typed value path for observation tokens" is prefigured by V-Steer (arXiv 2607.26228, COLM 2026): direct-logit-attribution picks heads where lower-privilege spans dominate, then multiplicatively edits cached value vectors at privileged vs conflicting spans per head, restoring instruction hierarchy on 7B-70B models; and CIV's FFN/residual trust gating covers the non-attention part. (3) The monitor channel (attention mass from action positions onto obs/usr/sys tokens, read by a weak classifier) is the mechanism of Attention Tracker (arXiv 2411.00348: training-free, attention on instruction vs injected content in "important heads", AUROC gains), RouteGuard (arXiv 2604.22888: response-time attention shift from trusted context to malicious skill spans, frozen-backbone detector fusing attention and hidden states on agent skill injection), Rennervate (arXiv 2512.08417, NDSS 2026: attentive pooling over heads and response tokens for token-level IPI detection, beats 15 defenses), and AgentWatcher (arXiv 2604.01194: attributes an agent's tool action to causal context segments on tool-use benchmarks). The "unverbalized influence is readable before generation" framing is also already established by Prompt Injection as Role Confusion (arXiv 2603.12277, ICML 2026), whose role probes predict attack success before the first token. (4) The Kevin arm (six-language cross-lingual instruction-hierarchy probe) is already the design of XIH-Bench (arXiv 2607.23545, EMNLP 2026: six languages, same- vs cross-language conflicts, Language Boundary Effect). (5) The motivating theory (control-path exposure through attention value aggregation; need for architectural instruction/data channel separation) is stated in arXiv 2606.27567. What remains after subtracting these is a recombination: soft learned type-pair biases + rank-8 typed value delta trained at 135M-0.6B, with six types instead of five and a receipts/reasoning type, evaluated with the existing monitor idea. That is an engineering comparison of soft vs hard provenance masking, not a new mechanism; it also fails the candidate's own kill condition framing since CIV already reports the hard-mask endpoint. Coverage limits: DuckDuckGo returned no results on all attempts and one OpenReview call timed out; full PDFs of CIV/V-Steer were not read, only abstracts plus the CIV README.

(2) SIM-CoT (2509.20317) aligns latent tokens with a decoder, but the decoder is co-trained and discarded at inference; no monitorability or attack evaluation. (3) PVG (2407.13692) trains legibility for a small verifier that is iteratively co-trained, on NL math. (4) Markovian Transformers (2404.18988, ICLR 2026) bound a NL CoT read by the same model, anti-steganography via KL prior; no external frozen reader, no rate matching. (5) New nearest threat surfaced this pass: 'Why Struggle with Continuous Latents? Interpretable Discrete Latent Reasoning via Rendered Compression' (2606.29712) builds a discrete latent vocabulary by clustering rendered-CoT image features and claims up to 20x compression with 'interpretable semantic structure', but the abstract reports no pre-committed frozen reader, no held-out monitor AUROC, no steganographic slack measurement, no obfuscation attack, no tool tasks. (6) DiscoLoop (2607.00341) loops discrete embeddings plus an unbounded continuous channel with no monitor, bound, or tool use; GRT (2608.15062) and looped tool-calling (2608.18171) keep continuous unprobed loop state; opaque-serial-depth (2603.09786) measures existing models and proposes no bandwidth-metered architecture; Thinking-States (2602.08332) uses token-form thoughts without any bit budget or monitor. (7) Supporting monitorability literature (Baker 2503.11926 monitorability tax/obfuscated reward hacking; 2607.09786 length penalties reduce hint detection 69->49%; 2510.27338 RL yields illegible CoT; 2506.01926 and NEST 2602.14095 steganographic CoT) motivates but does not build the proposed medium. Caveats lowering confidence: the mechanism is a recombination of known parts (frozen-listener grounding from emergent communication, monitor-in-reward from Baker et al., reserved-vocabulary code from Abstract-CoT, discrete loop channel from DiscoLoop); the novelty is in the design constraint (pre-committed frozen weaker reader + rate matching + measured collusion slack + metered C-bit register file) and its measurement, not a new operator, so a reviewer could call it incremental. Coverage limits: OpenReview forum and API pages are CAPTCHA-blocked from this route (four hits unread); DuckDuckGo timed out twice; only abstracts were read (no full text), so 2606.29712 and 2604.04902 could contain a frozen-decoder or adversarial section not visible in the abstract. The pilot as written cannot separate the claimed mechanism (frozen, weaker, pre-committed reader + rate-matched codebook) from cheaper explanations, and its headline effects are largely fixed by the evaluation design.

(1) Metric-equals-objective circularity. The policy is rewarded with lambda_R log p_R(m|z) for the exact variables m (next tool, argument slots, hint-use, constraint violation) that the "held-out" monitor is then scored on. Monitorability so defined is guaranteed by training; the explicit-CoT control gets r_task only, so "anchored code >= 90% of explicit-CoT monitorability" compares a trained-for-metric arm against an untrained one, read by a deliberately weak (20M/135M) NL monitor that understates NL monitorability. 2603.30036's own authors could not test whether an "aligned" CoT reward improves monitorability because the monitored variable was the trained variable; 2512.00218 found direct monitorability optimization "did not reliably improve monitorability" once the monitor variable is fixed. The design also forecloses the one property that makes legibility training valuable in NL (VFT, 2506.22777: verbalization generalizes to new reward hacks): with T log2 K = H(m) + eps, nothing outside pre-specified m can be exposed, so on any novel misbehavior the abstract medium is unmonitorable by construction while NL CoT is not — the comparison metric excludes exactly that case.

(2) Missing factorial cell / strongest control absent. The arms vary medium without reader (length-penalized CoT, Abstract-CoT-style code) and reader without changing medium (reader-strength ladder), but no arm is NL tokens + the same frozen reader term on m + the same T-token cap, and no arm is a rate-matched structured self-report ("tool=search; hint=used; violation=none") with the same reward. Markovian Transformers (2404.18988) use the same model as reader on the answer, not a frozen weak reader on m, so it does not fill the cell. Either missing arm would match the anchored code on monitorability, compression and slack with zero architectural content, so nothing in the pilot attributes any effect to the codebook or to the reader being frozen/weaker.

(3) The slack claim is a capacity ledger, not a mechanism. I(z;s) <= eps + H(m|z) follows from H(z) <= T log2 K for any channel of that size; "less steganographic slack than NL CoT" is "fewer bits than NL CoT", and the unconstrained-code control differs only in not being forced to spend H(m) bits on m. The controls are matched in tokens, not bits (a 50k-vocab token carries ~15.6 bits vs 6 for K=64), so the P2 collusion-probe gaps (<= eps+2 vs >= 16 vs >= 12 bits) are predicted by the ledger alone.

(4) Held-out-monitor leakage and the co-trained-arm prediction. The frozen reader is a linear head over gloss-initialized codebook embeddings; against a fixed linear reader the GRPO optimum is a lookup table m -> z*, so z carries exactly m (H(z|m) ~ 0): a label, not a reasoning medium. "Gloss rendering" decodes with the reader's own dictionary, so the post-hoc monitor shares the reader's function class. Any deterministic co-trained code is equally decodable by a monitor trained on disjoint (z, m) pairs; the predicted anchored 0.85 vs co-trained <= 0.70 gap can only arise from monitor capacity/data — an evaluation choice, not a property of frozen vs co-trained (cf. 2608.04928: decoder-rendered latents close the monitor gap when the relevant content is in the trace; monitorability tracks task and access, not medium).

(5) Action-copy shortcut and the rewrite-attack result. Two of the four monitor variables (next tool, argument slots) are a copy of the action emitted immediately after z, so aggregate AUROC and the re-encoder-attack robustness are dominated by variables that cannot be rewritten without changing the action — the same "false average" 2608.00583 documents (aggregate accuracy dominated by hacks the actions give away; reasoning-only rewrites drop catch rate 95% -> <11%). P1/P2 do not pre-register per-variable AUROC for hint-use and constraint violation, the only safety-relevant bits. With T=8, K=64 there is no capacity for computation in z, so the medium is CoT-as-rationalization in Emmons et al.'s sense (2507.05246) and the tasks must be solvable without it; latent placeholders exploiting shortcuts is the documented failure mode (2512.21711).

(6) Substrate B accuracy(C) is not identified. The "human-renderable" register file carries T*S*log2|V_reg| = 8*4*10.97 ~ 351 bits/iteration, more than the metered channel at C=32 (256 bits) and infinitely more at C=0; anchoring registers to R_phi constrains only their m-content, so loop state can route through registers as an encoded NL-token channel (2310.18512), producing "gain survives at C <= 32" and the register-monitor AUROC on m simultaneously. Measuring eps_reg afterwards reports the leak but does not restore identification. The knee location is a property of ToyTools' working-memory demand, which the same team designs: 2605.30757 shows a compressed loop is limited by recurrent-state size and performance depends on whether the persistent-state budget matches task demand, and that full sequence-state loops (the Huginn/Ouro "continuous loop" control) are a different regime — so continuous-vs-metered confounds bandwidth with compressed-vs-sequence-state, discretization noise and straight-through gradients; a bandwidth-matched compressed continuous control is absent. VQ codebooks at 2^C entries add an optimization confound (collapse, commitment/reseeding machinery; 2309.15505), and looped arms at identical architecture/accuracy land in different dynamical phases by initialization (2608.26556), so "no stable training after two remediation rounds" conflates optimization with capacity. The Qwen3-0.6B recurrence-adapter retrofit lists no same-size scratchpad/iso-param control (cf. 2608.11233).

Net: the two decisive comparisons (anchored vs explicit CoT on m; metered vs continuous loop) each lack the matched control that would isolate the stated mechanism, and the strongest cheap controls (rate-matched self-report with the same reward; registers disabled or bandwidth-matched continuous slots) would be expected to reproduce the predicted effects.
